text:
jason: Heads-up — Support got an escalation: Dedicated dashboard for cluster prod-dedicated-eu shows 0 GPUs after the cluster rename this morning. Customer is seeing OOM fallbacks.
elaine: I can see the alert. UI shows node list empty but the k8s cluster has 8 nodes according to kube-api.
matt: Did the rename change any node labels or nodepool ids? That tends to break our inventory mapping.
derek: Support says rename was from prod-dedicated-eu -> prod-dedicated-eu-1 (minor suffix). Node labels were updated via a staged job.
jason: Running an inventory API call now: `curl -sS https://internal-api.redwood/api/v1/dedicated/clusters/prod-dedicated-eu-1/nodes | jq '.'` -> returns `[]` (200).
elaine: Huh returns 200 with empty array. Check service logs for inventory-sync.
inventory-sync-bot: inventory-sync service restarted at 2025-10-31T08:10:12Z due to kube probe failure.
matt: Logs: `KeyError: 'cluster_name'` in inventory-sync on rename handler around 08:09. Looks like the rename led to a missing mapping key.
derek: Also seeing a bunch of 429s from k8s API in the same window — rate limiting during the relabel job. Could have caused partial updates + crash.
jason: Repro steps I ran locally: 1) rename cluster name in infra API 2) run node relabel job 3) observe inventory-sync pod OOM/crashloop + cluster mapping dropped.
elaine: Can we reindex quick? There's a backfill endpoint: `POST /internal/inventory/reindex?cluster=prod-dedicated-eu-1` but it requires auth + service token.
matt: I'm gonna trigger the backfill from bastion with service token. Will post status.
support: Customer still impacted, reported increased latency on inference calls. They asked for ETA.
jason: Noted. Keep them updated.
inventory-sync-bot: reindex job queued (job_id=ri-20251031-88).
matt: Reindex started. I see it fetching nodes from kube-api directly and inserting to inventory DB. No more KeyError after we applied a small patch to tolerate old/new cluster_name fields.
derek: Patch diff: `if not cluster_name: cluster_name = metadata.get('displayName')` — small guard but worked.
matt: Backfill completed. DB shows 8 node docs reinserted.
jason: UI cache invalidation: hitting `/console/cache/invalidate?scope=cluster:prod-dedicated-eu-1`. Doing that now.
elaine: After cache invalidation, dashboard shows correct GPU counts and node pool breakdown. I also see the historical metrics are delayed — Prometheus exporter had a 15m scrape gap during the incident.
derek: We should surface that to the customer: node inventory restored but some recent token-level latency/cost breakdowns may be missing for ~15 minutes.
support: Relay to customer: inventory restored, workloads should be stable, small window (08:05-08:20 UTC) of missing metrics; escalation closed if no regressions.
jason: Plan for follow-up: 1) make inventory-sync tolerant of missing cluster_name 2) add a retry/backoff for relabel job to avoid simultaneous rate spikes to kube-api 3) add an alert if inventory-sync writes 0 nodes for an active cluster for >2 min.
matt: I'll open a PR for the KeyError guard and add a unit test.
derek: I'll add backoff to the relabel job and put a quote in runbook about rate limits.
jason: Thanks. Closing loop: support informed customer and asked to reopen if anything else. Marking this thread resolved. :thumbsup:
